concept: Queryable Encryption contention and range-index tuning
summary: Source-anchored research for Queryable Encryption contention and range-index tuning. Run status: COMPLETED.

facts.text: Contention is not a general protection against leakage abuse: the 2023 ETH analysis of preview-era equality QE found that query logs could reunite values across contention tokens. That result is historical evidence, not a demonstrated attack on current range-index tuning. (low confidence)
Set realistic inclusive min/max bounds to improve range efficiency; use the field's BSON type. Bounds are required when precision is specified. (high confidence)

SERVER-92390 documents a historical small-domain failure: an unspecified trimFactor with a domain of six or fewer bits could produce 'Trim factor must be less than the number of bits used to represent the domain.' The tracker lists fixes in 8.0.0-rc14 and 8.1.0-rc0; this is not evidence of a current unfixed defect. (low confidence)
Contention partitions per-value counters into randomly selected slots; increasing it reduces collisions for concurrent same-value writes but increases read work. (high confidence)

Queryable Encryption partitions each field/value counter into contention + 1 slots and randomly selects a slot on insertion, reducing conflicts between concurrent writes of repeated values. (high confidence)
trimFactor removes root levels from the encrypted range tree. Raising it reduces write conflicts and improves insert throughput, while slowing broad range reads. (high confidence)

Lower sparsity produces faster range queries with greater metadata storage overhead. MongoDB documents default 2 and a maximum increase from 4 to 8 in version 8.2; current repository validation permits 1–8. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14)
For double/decimal fields, precision truncates query digits without rounding or altering the stored encrypted value; reducing precision limits index overhead. (low confidence)
The consulted manual specifies defaults contention=8, sparsity=2 and trimFactor=6; SERVER-91077 records the latter two defaults. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-27)

Explicit-encryption RangeOpts must match the destination encryptedFields configuration for min, max, trimFactor, sparsity and precision; double/decimal128 min/max/precision must be supplied together or all omitted. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-27)
Spring Data MongoDB 5.0 documents range configuration through @RangeEncrypted with contentionFactor and rangeOptions, including bounds and floating-point precision examples. (low confidence)

Spring Data MongoDB exposes range configuration through @RangeEncrypted and collection options. Its examples combine contentionFactor=8 with integer bounds 0–150, and use typed BSON bounds for decimal-valued fields. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-23)
Omit a query type for encrypted fields that never need encrypted searches to avoid generating their searchable indexes. (medium confidence)
The documented automatic-encryption contention default is 8; the server configuration also declares 8. Explicit encryption requires a contention value. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14)

Treat database snapshots accompanied by query transcripts/logs as outside current QE security guarantees, especially for range queries. The historical ETH study illustrates why logs require a separate threat-model review; increasing tuning parameters does not establish protection against this adversary. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14)
